assumptions: Synthetic fixtures exercise first usable project-file selection: context/product-marketing.md, reports/GROWTH_ONBOARDING_PLAN.md, brand/BRAND.md, legacy BRAND.md, then wiki/INDEX.md. The workflow does not blend product identities.

A project without one of those usable files may supply context_text. The current writing-style guide is optional. The calendar remains an editable suggestion, not a posting schedule or evidence of a product claim.
Offline checks verify budget, shape and bounded text. They do not measure live model quality, actual supplier cost or social performance.
cost_drivers: One gpt-6-sol model call with up to 32000 serialized input bytes and 4096 output tokens; project context and current writing style drive input size.
effects: Writes one reviewable social/PLAN.md project file. No social platform connection, post, scheduled publication or external delivery occurs.

cases.description: A current context file produces three to five weighted pillars and a calendar whose slots fit the weekly hours.
Supplied context supports planning when the known project context files are absent.

inputs.context_text: A small software team offers a traceable CSV import for product analytics. Each imported row retains a link to its source record, and validation keeps invalid rows out of charts. The product is for teams that need to check a number before using a chart to make a decision.

rubric.question: Are the audience, pillars and ideas faithful to the selected current product context, with uncertain facts called out rather than invented?
Can the founder realistically draft, engage and review signals within the stated weekly hours?
Does each platform choice fit the audience, and are the calendar ideas distinct enough to draft as separate posts?
